title: Commitment Scheduler & Resilience Lattice — Q2 Dedicated Capacity Roadmap
creator: Priya Malik
description:
Overview: Build the Commitment Scheduler and a resilience lattice that let Dedicated customers define flexible reservation windows, hedged warm pools, and graceful capacity fallthroughs. This ticket captures the Q2 roadmap slice: design policy primitives, wire them into autoscale decisioning, and add observability + OKR metrics for adoption and cost control.

Why now: Customers increasingly need predictable throughput with lower unit cost while tolerating brief fallbacks during demand spikes. Current Dedicated controls are rigid and make customers overcommit; the scheduler and lattice will reduce waste while providing clear SLAs and runbooked fallback behaviours.

Goals and success metrics (OKR mapped):
- Objective: Reduce average dedicated reservation overcommit by 20% while preserving 99% of customer latency SLOs.
- KR1: 20% reduction in committed but unused GPU hours across pilot customers by end of Q2.
- KR2: 95% of pilot requests served within p99 latency SLO when using hedged warm-pool fallback.
- KR3: Two pilot customers onboarded to the Commitment Scheduler and provide adoption feedback.

Scope and deliverables (Q2 slice):
- Policy primitives for time-windowed reservations, hedging factor, and fastpath failover priority.
- Autoscaler integration: scheduler outputs capacity windows + hedging budget to Dedicated autoscaler engine.
- Resilience lattice rules: A small policy DSL that composes fallback tiers (primary reserved pool -> warm pool -> burst reservoir -> fallback model).
- Console UI mockups and rollout controls for policy creation, preview, and simulated cost estimates.
- Telemetry: per-policy utilization, wasted hours, fallback frequency, and end-to-end latency impact dashboards.
- Pilot onboarding runbook and billing implications document.

Milestones and timeline: 
- Feb week 1–2: Design spike and policy DSL proposal (UX, infra API contract).
- Feb week 3–Mar week 1: Eng spike to implement autoscaler hooks and simulator for policy behaviour.
- Mar week 2: Console prototypes + PRD alignment with Solutions Eng.
- Mar week 3–Apr week 2: Implementation sprint 1 (policy storage, orchestration API).
- Apr week 3–May week 4: Integration sprint (autoscaler + runtime), telemetry + dashboards.
- May week 4: Pilot enablement with 2 customers.

Trade-offs and decisions to be made: 
- Strict SLO vs cost: conservative hedging reduces customer cost but can increase fallbacks; we will default to conservative hedging for trial and allow more aggressive defaults for self-serve customers.
- Complexity of DSL: prefer a compact composable lattice over full policy language to keep UI simple and audit-friendly.
- Billing model: evaluate meter for hedged warm pool usage vs committed reservation uplift; final billing to be decided with Finance.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Incorrect hedging heuristics cause increased p99 latency for production traffic. Mitigation: start with simulation-and-rehearsal mode and gradual canary rollout tied to latency alarm triggers.
- Risk: Cross-region capacity constraints break fallback sequencing. Mitigation: add region-aware routing and an explicit policy constraint that tags fallback tiers with regions.
- Risk: Customer confusion about new reservation windows. Mitigation: clear console previews, cost estimates, and a 30-day guided pilot with Solutions Eng.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Policy DSL v0 implemented and persisted in platform config with validation rules.
- Autoscaler reads policy windows and applies hedging budget during allocation decisions.
- Console allows creation of policy and shows projected cost delta within 5% of simulator.
- Telemetry streams created and dashboards show utilization and fallback metrics for pilot customers.
- Pilot runbook documented and two pilot customers successfully onboarded with measurable metrics.
